body:
_Migrated from issue #1360, filed 2026-08-04._

## Symptom

Drop books into the ingest folder while the container is stopped — or while it is still starting — and they are never imported. They sit in the folder indefinitely. Touching them again later (re-copying, renaming) imports them normally, so the books themselves are fine.

Most likely to bite when you copy a batch in and restart to pick up a new image, or when an external sync writes into the folder while the container is down.

## Cause

`cwa-ingest-service` is purely event-driven on the inotify path. `root/etc/s6-overlay/s6-rc.d/cwa-ingest-service/run` ends with:

```
s6-setuidgid abc inotifywait -m -r --format="%e %w%f" -e close_write -e moved_to -e create "$WATCH_FOLDER" | \
while read -r events filepath; do
        handle_event "$filepath" "$events"
done
```

`inotifywait` reports only events that occur after its watches exist, and there is no startup scan of `$WATCH_FOLDER`. A file already present when the service starts generated its event before anything was listening, so `handle_event` is never called for it and nothing retries.

`has_pending_ingest_files()` does exist but is only read inside `is_ingest_batch_quiet()`, as a condition for the *post-batch follow-up* — it gates cleanup work, it does not enqueue unprocessed files. `process_retry_queue` only replays the persisted queue, which a never-seen file was never added to.

## Not universal

The polling fallback does not have this gap, because it compares directory listings rather than waiting on events. So this affects the default inotify path only, and is masked for anyone on:

- `NETWORK_SHARE_MODE=true`
- `CWA_WATCH_MODE=poll`
- Docker Desktop (auto-detected via `is_docker_desktop`)

which is likely why it has stayed quiet — several maintainer/dev setups take the fallback path.

## How it surfaced

The SPA e2e job hits the same gap from the other side. Its seed step waits only for the web app to answer HTTP, then copies five books in; when `cwa-ingest-service` had not yet established its watches, the run failed `ingest imported only 0 of 5 seed books` with watches established, no ingest activity, and no `New file detected` line ([run 30866805515](https://github.com/new-usemame/Calibre-Web-NextGen/actions/runs/30866805515) 0/5 vs [30868527022](https://github.com/new-usemame/Calibre-Web-NextGen/actions/runs/30868527022) 5/5, same step 34 minutes apart). #1359 works around it in the harness by waiting for the watcher and re-nudging missed files; that is a test-harness workaround and does nothing for real installs.

## Suggested fix

Sweep the watch folder once, after the watches are established, and hand any supported file already sitting there to `handle_event` (or straight to the retry queue). Doing it after the watch is set up rather than before avoids a new gap; the existing `is_recent_duplicate_event` / processing-marker guards should keep a file that also fired a real event from being processed twice.

`has_pending_ingest_files()` already knows how to enumerate exactly the right set, so the sweep is mostly a matter of reusing it.

## Not verified

Reported from reading the service script and the CI signature, not from a reproduction on a real install with a restart. Worth confirming that way before fixing.
title: Books already in the ingest folder when the container starts are never imported
